description: A sugar or syrup added to the food. Labels use many different names for sugars (e.g. dextrose, glucose syrup, invert syrup, maltose).
A sweetener other than sugar: an intense sweetener (e.g. sucralose) or a polyol / sugar alcohol (e.g. sorbitol).
An oil or fat, e.g. palm oil, palmolein, vegetable fat, butter or ghee.
A food additive whose main function is preservation: it helps protect food against spoilage by micro-organisms.
A food additive that adds or restores colour.
A food additive with an INS/E number. Its function is shown where the label or the reference data states it.
An additive code. INS (International Numbering System, Codex Alimentarius) and E-numbers (EU) use the same numbers, e.g. INS 330 = E330 = citric acid.
The functional class written on the label (e.g. 'acidity regulator', 'emulsifier'). It tells what job the additive next to it does.
A flavouring: natural, nature-identical or artificial flavouring substances.
A food ingredient (e.g. wheat flour, milk solids, salt, spices).
